UNITED STATES COURT OF INTERNATIONAL TRADE

GAMECHANGE SOLAR CORP.,

Plaintiff,

v.

UNITED STATES,

Defendant.
Before: Timothy C. Stanceu, Judge

Court No. 24-00174

OPINION

[Denying plaintiff’s motion for judgment on the
items.summary: The Court of International Trade denied GameChange Solar Corp.'s challenge to an International Trade Administration determination that the company's off-grid solar charging module is within the scope of antidumping and countervailing duty orders on crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells from China. The court found that the charging module, which contains crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells and is described by GameChange as a module, falls within the scope language covering modules of such cells assembled into other products. The court rejected GameChange's arguments that the product qualified for a consumer good exclusion or an off-grid photovoltaic panel exclusion.

items.summary: The Tenth Circuit held en banc that in a prosecution under 18 U.S.C. § 1152 where the victim is an Indian, the defendant's Indian status constitutes an affirmative defense that the defendant must prove by a preponderance of the evidence. items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–36: To amend the Fair Credit Reporting Act to prevent consumer reporting agencies from furnishing consumer reports under certain circumstances, and for other purposes. Public Law 36 Public Law 119–36 139 Stat. 493 2025-09-05
items.summary: Public Law 119-36, the Homebuyers Privacy Protection Act, amends the Fair Credit Reporting Act to restrict consumer reporting agencies from furnishing consumer reports in certain circumstances related to residential mortgage lending. The law prohibits furnishing such reports based on a prescreening request connected to a mortgage loan transaction unless the requesting entity either holds documented consumer authorization, has originated or services the consumer's mortgage, or is a depository institution with a current account for that consumer. The law also requires the Comptroller General to study the value of trigger leads received by text message and report findings to Congress within 12 months of enactment.
items.title: Public Law 119–36: To amend the Fair Credit Reporting Act to prevent consumer reporting agencies from furnishing consumer reports under certain circumstances, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–120: To require an annual report of taxpayer-funded projects that are over budget and behind schedule. Public Law 120 Public Law 119–120 140 Stat. 1065 2026-10-07 2026-10-07 United States Government Publishing Office National
items.summary: Public Law 119-120, titled the "Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act of 2025" and enacted on October 7, 2026, requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to establish guidance for federal agencies to submit annual reports on taxpayer-funded projects that are more than 5 years behind schedule or exceed their original cost estimate by $1 billion or more. The Director must compile agency submissions into an annual report to Congress and post it on the OMB website, including project descriptions, locations, contractors, scope changes, current timelines and costs, and explanations for delays or cost increases. The guidance must be issued within one year of the law's enactment.
items.title: Public Law 119–120: To require an annual report of taxpayer-funded projects that are over budget and behind schedule.

items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus SAS Model A318 series airplanes; Model A319 series airplanes; Model A320 series airplanes; and Model A321 series airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of door evacuation slide systems failing to inflate during emergency evacuations, due to the fracture and separation of the connector on the inflation hose assembly. This proposed AD would require the replacement of each affected slide with a serviceable slide. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts. items.summary: EPA is issuing significant new use rules (SNURs) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for certain chemical substances that were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs) and are also subject to an Order issued by EPA pursuant to TSCA. The SNURs require persons to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing the manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or processing of any of these chemical substances for an activity that is designated as a significant new use in the SNUR. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the conditions of that use for that chemical substance. In addition, the manufacture or processing for the significant new use may not commence until EPA has conducted a review of the required notification; made an appropriate determination regarding that notification; and taken such actions as required by that determination.
items.title: Significant New Use Rules on Certain Chemical Substances (26-1)

items.summary: In the Notice section of today's Federal Register , the Office of Justice Programs (OJP), a component within the United States Department of Justice (DOJ or Department), has published a notice of a new system of records, Bureau of Justice Statistics (BJS) Statistical Data, JUSTICE/OJP-017, for the statistical data collections that BJS conducts under 34 U.S.C. 10132. In this notice of proposed rulemaking, the OJP proposes to exempt this system of records from certain provisions of the Privacy Act in order to comply with the confidentiality provisions of 34 U.S.C. 10231 and 34 U.S.C. 30303 and the requirement of 34 U.S.C. 10134 that the data are to be used solely for statistical or research purposes. Additionally, data are to be used for authorized purposes under the Prison Rape Elimination Act of 2003 (PREA; 44 U.S.C. 3563) and the Death in Custody Reporting Act of 2013 (DCRA; Pub. L. 113-242). Consistent with the data use requirements set forth in 34 U.S.C. 10134, no adverse determinations are made from these records as to any identifiable individual. items.summary: The Federal Maritime Commission (Commission) proposes to adjust or meet unfavorable shipping conditions created by the Government of Spain. The Commission proposes a per-voyage fee on all Spanish vessels of $200,000 and restrictions on the import of certain Spanish goods into the United States. The Commission also proposes using additional statutory authority to impose these remedies because the Government of Spain has unduly impaired the access of U.S. flag vessels to trade between foreign ports. The Commission herein offers an opportunity for a public hearing. The Commission invites public comment on all aspects of this proposed rule.

items.summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is proposing to adopt as final the revisions to the Central Liquidity Facility (CLF) rule made under two interim final rules (IFRs) published in the Federal Register on April 29, 2020, and March 24, 2021. The proposal would adopt the amendments made by these IFRs and, where appropriate, would remove provisions from the NCUA's regulations that have lapsed under the terms of the IFRs. The proposal would also remove or modify certain filing requirements and criteria the Board uses to approve CLF members. Finally, the proposal would amend the timing requirements related to pay adjustments to the capital stock subscription, clarify various regulatory provisions, and make necessary conforming edits.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-11812; Project Identifier MCAI-2025-01222-R] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Helicopters AGEN
items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model MBB-BK 117 D-2 helicopters. This proposed AD was prompted by certification test results of a certain common cargo hook beam (CCHB) on the affected helicopters, which revealed that the installed CCHB could result in fuel leakage following a survivable accident. This proposed AD would require modification of the CCHB and fuel system and installation of structural reinforcement. This proposed AD would also prohibit installing a certain CCHB on any helicopter. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Helicopters
